title: GM Toolkit campaign export (format version 1)
description: Documents the shape produced/accepted by GmToolkit.Core.Import.CampaignExportDto (M5 -- see ROADMAP.md and issue #129). This file is documentation only: nothing in GM Toolkit loads or validates against it at runtime today. GmToolkit.Core.Import.ImportValidator is the runtime validator, and its rules are the authoritative ones if the two ever disagree -- keep this file in sync with GmToolkit.Core.Import.CampaignExportDto/PlayerCharacterExportDto/NpcExportDto whenever their shape changes.

formatVersion.description: The only value this build of GM Toolkit produces or accepts. A reader that doesn't recognize a higher formatVersion must refuse to import the file rather than guess at its shape -- mirrors the CharacterSystem pack format's own formatVersion convention (see SYSTEMS.md).

name.description: The campaign's name. Required, non-blank, and at most 200 characters -- matches Campaign.NameMaxLength. Used as the stable identifier for conflict detection on re-import; the campaign's own database id is deliberately never part of this format (see the 'No database ids' note below).

gameSystem.description: Free text, e.g. 'D&D 5e' -- matches Campaign.GameSystem. Not validated against any fixed list; the app does not model rules systems beyond this label plus the optional characterSystemId below.

characterSystemId.description: The id of a typed CharacterSystem stat schema pack (e.g. 'dnd5e-2024'), or null for a freeform campaign with no schema attached -- matches Campaign.CharacterSystemId. Not a database foreign key: an importer should look this id up in its own installed CharacterSystem registry and treat an unresolvable id as a validation error (or fall back to freeform), never as a hard parse failure.

exportedUtc.description: UTC timestamp of when this export file was produced. Describes the export file itself, not any entity inside it -- this format deliberately carries no createdUtc/lastOpenedUtc for the campaign, or createdUtc for any NPC, since those describe a specific database's copy of the data, not the campaign's own content.

playerCharacters.description: Every player character in the campaign. Order is not significant; each entry's own characterName is the stable identifier used for per-character conflict detection on import.

npcs.description: Every NPC in the campaign. Order is not significant; each entry's own name is the stable identifier used for per-NPC conflict detection on import.

characterName.description: Required, non-blank, at most 200 characters -- matches PlayerCharacter.NameMaxLength. The stable identifier for this character across export/import.

level.description: A negative level is rejected by GmToolkit.Core.Import.ImportValidator; there is otherwise no fixed upper bound, since level/tier conventions vary by system.

stats.description: System-agnostic key/value bag -- matches PlayerCharacter.Stats. The GM (or an attached characterSystemId schema) defines the keys; every value is stored as a string regardless of its logical type (number, boolean, enum choice, etc.). Passive values a GM looks up mid-session (perception, AC, etc.) are just well-known keys in this same bag, not their own fields.

name.description: Required, non-blank, at most 200 characters -- matches Npc.NameMaxLength. The stable identifier for this NPC across export/import.

wasGenerated.description: True when this NPC originally came out of the generator (see the NPC generator milestone, M3).

stats.description: System-agnostic key/value bag -- matches Npc.Stats. Same shape/rules as playerCharacters[].stats above.
